what_happened: A docs job to correct and complete the firstmate explainer page to reach a score of 4 of 5 was rejected. The final verdict was fail. The verifier changed its snapshot during verification, which the system treated as a blocker because it invalidates the verdict. No acceptance criterion or check is listed as unmet. The job was rejected because the verdict could not be trusted, not because the page was shown to be wrong.
cause: The verifier runs with write access to the same snapshot it judges, and nothing enforces that the snapshot is read-only or compares a fingerprint before and after. The only detection is a late finding at the end, so a verification run can invalidate itself and waste the whole job. The vague quality target (reach 4 of 5) may also have led the verifier to try to fix or regenerate things while judging, but the record does not confirm this.
prevention: Run the verifier against a read-only snapshot, for example a read-only mount or a copy with write permissions removed. Hash the snapshot before and after verification. If the hashes differ, discard that verdict and automatically re-run verification once on a fresh snapshot copy, rather than rejecting the job. Any scratch output the verifier needs goes in a separate writable directory outside the snapshot.
proposed_request: Make verification tamper-proof: the verifier must judge a read-only snapshot and write only to a separate scratch directory. Record a content hash of the snapshot before and after each verification. If the hash changes, the verdict is void and verification re-runs once on a fresh copy. Only a second change rejects the job, with the diff of changed files in the finding. Add a test where a verifier modifies the snapshot and shows that the first run is voided and the retry runs. Then re-run the firstmate explainer page job (correct and complete the page to reach 4 of 5) to confirm it gets a valid verdict.
